<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par52 />{{GHGheb|text=עִנֵּן|translate=to gather the clouds together}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עָנָן}}), {{GHGheb|text=שִׁלֵּשׁ|translate=to divide in three parts}}, or ''to do a thing for the third time'' (from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁלשׁ}}); probably also {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר|translate=to speak}}, from {{GHGheb|text=דָּבָר|translate=a word}}. Or again, the denominative may express taking away, injuring, &c., the object denoted by the noun (''privative Piʿēl'', cf. our ''to skin, to behead, to bone''), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁרֵשׁ}}, from {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁ֫רֶשׁ|translate=to root out, to extirpate}}, {{GHGheb|text=זִנֵּב}} prop. to ''injure the tail'' ({{GHGheb|text=זָנָב}}), hence ''to rout the rear'' of an army, ''to attack it''; {{GHGheb|text=לִבֵּב|translate=to ravish the heart}}; {{GHGheb|text=דִּשֵּׁן|translate=to remove the ashes}} ({{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫שֶׁן}}), {{GHGheb|text=חִטֵּא|translate=to free from sin}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֵטְא}}), {{GHGheb|text=עִצֵּם}} ''to break any one’s bones'' ({{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶם}}; cf., in the same sense, {{GHGheb|text=גֵּרֵם}} from {{GHGheb|text=גֶּ֫רֶם}}); {{GHGheb|text=סֵעֵף|translate=to lop the boughs}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=33}} (from {{GHGheb|text=סְעִיף|translate=a bough}}). Some words are clearly denominatives, although the noun from which they are derived is no longer found, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סִקֵּל|translate=to stone, to pelt with stones}} (also used in this sense in {{GHGterm|Qal}}), and ''to remove stones'' (from a field), ''to clear away stones''; cf. our ''to stone'', used also in the sense of ''taking out the stones'' from fruit.

The meaning of the {{GHGterm|passive}} ({{GHGterm|Puʿal}}) follows naturally from the above, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בִּקֵּשׁ}} Piʿēl ''to seek'', Puʿal ''to be sought''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|i}}
In {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} the literal, concrete meaning of the verb has sometimes been retained, when {{GHGterm|Qal}} has acquired a figurative sense, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּלָה}}, Piʿēl ''to uncover'', Qal ''to reveal'', also ''to emigrate'', i.e. to make the land bare.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|k}}
Also with an intransitive sense {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} occurs as an intensive form, but only in poetic language, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חתת}} in Piʿēl ''to be broken in pieces'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=56}}; {{GHGheb|text=פִּחַד|translate=to tremble}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=28|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=רִוָּה|translate=to be drunken}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=5.7}}; [{{GHGheb|text=מִעֵט|translate=to be few}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=3}}]; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=60|verse=11|hidebook=1}} instead of the Piʿēl of {{GHGheb|text=פתח}} the Niphʿal is certainly to be read, with Cheyne.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|l}}
Rem. 1. The (more frequent) form of the perfect with {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the second syllable appears especially before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=9|hidebook=1}}) and in the middle of sentences in continuous discourse, but at the end of the sentence (in {{GHGterm|pause}}) the form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} is more common. Cf. {{GHGheb|text=גִּדֵּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=21}} with {{GHGheb|text=גִּדַּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=מִלֵּט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=5}} with {{GHGheb|text=מִלַּט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִצַּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=16}} with {{GHGheb|text=קִצֵּץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=129|verse=4}}; but Qameṣ never appears in this pausal form. The ''3rd sing. fem.'' in {{GHGterm|pause}} is always of the form {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּ֫לָה}}, except {{GHGheb|text=קִבָּ֫צָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=7}}; the 3rd plur. always as {{GHGheb|text=קִטֵּ֫לוּ}}; the ''2nd'' and ''1st sing.'' and ''1st plur.'' of course as {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְתָּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְתִּי}} (but always {{GHGheb|text=דִּבַּֽרְתִּי}} and {{GHGheb|text=לִמַּ֫דְתִּי}}), {{GHGheb|text=קִטָּ֫לְנוּ}}. In the ''3rd sing. perf.'' {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר|translate=to speak}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּפֶּר|translate=to pardon}}, and {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֶּס|translate=to wash clothes}} (also {{GHGheb|text=כִבֵּס}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=11}}) take {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, but become in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֵּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּבֵּס}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=25}}); the ''pausal'' form of {{GHGheb|text=כִּפֶּר}} does not occur.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|m}}
{{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} in the first syllable (as in Aramaic and Arabic) occurs only once, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=51}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫שַּׁנִי|translate=he made me forget}}, to emphasize more clearly the play on the name {{GHGheb|text=מְנַשֶּׁה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|52|n}}
2. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (and {{GHGterm|jussive}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=25}}), ''infinitive, and imperative Piʿēl'' (as also in {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}) the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} in the final syllable, when followed by {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}}, is usually shortened into {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְבַקֶּשׁ־לוֹ|translate=he seeks for himself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=קַדֶּשׁ־לִי|translate=sanctify unto me}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=2}}. ''Pausal-forms'' with {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} instead of {{GHGterm|Ṣere}}, as {{GHGheb|text=יְרַחֶף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲרַחֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=6}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=6}} in the infinitive, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=9}} in the participle), owe their origin to some particular school of Masoretes, and are wrongly accepted by Baer; cf. the analogous cases in {{GHGpar|75|n}} and hh. If the final syllable of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} has Pathaḥ (before a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}}), it remains<section end=par52 /><noinclude>
